five_minutes: Hawkish commentary from the Fed around Jackson Hole raises rate hike risks, pushing US Treasury yields higher and threatening FII outflows.
India's July industrial output eased to 6.7% as a 16.1% surge in capital goods was partially offset by a 1% contraction in consumer non-durables.
A US-brokered agreement granting access to 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan crude introduces long-term supply expansion to global oil markets.
State governments are set to raise ₹27,000 crore via RBI bond auctions, adding fresh sovereign supply at the long end of the yield curve.
The Finance Ministry has scheduled pre-Budget 2027 consultations starting October 12, focusing on spending control and revenue targets.

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: Hawkish Fed rhetoric lifts Treasury yields and elevates risk of renewed FII pressure on Indian equities
items.what_happened: Kevin Warsh stated that the Federal Reserve still has work to do if inflation does not ease, with markets pricing in a 34% probability of a rate hike at the September 15-16 meeting.
items.why_it_matters: A hawkish repricing of US monetary policy lifts US Treasury yields and strengthens the USD, narrowing rate differentials and creating headwinds for FII equity flows into India.
items.action: Recheck interest rate sensitivity assumptions across banking and export portfolio holdings ahead of the mid-September FOMC.

items.headline: SEC proposal to exempt EU sovereign debt widens US institutional access to European fixed income
items.what_happened: The US Securities and Exchange Commission proposed amending Exchange Act Rule 3a12-8 to add European Union debt obligations to the exempted foreign government debt list.
items.why_it_matters: Reduces trading frictions and reporting overhead for US-based asset managers dealing in EU supranational bonds, facilitating cross-border fixed-income allocations.

items.headline: India's July IIP moderates to 6.7% as robust capex contrasts with persistent rural and consumer drag
items.what_happened: India's industrial output growth slowed to 6.7% in July from 7.3% in June, driven by a 16.1% expansion in capital goods while consumer non-durables contracted by 1.0%.
items.why_it_matters: The wide divergence confirms that the corporate and infrastructure investment cycle remains intact, but weakness in mass consumption will continue to weigh on FMCG volume growth.

items.headline: Exporters seek cotton yarn export curbs as input cost surge threatens textile margins
items.what_happened: The Apparel Export Promotion Council urged the Commerce Ministry to regulate cotton yarn exports to counter sharp domestic price spikes harming garment export competitiveness.
items.why_it_matters: Any trade intervention or export restriction would compress margins for yarn spinners while providing cost relief to downstream apparel manufacturers.

items.headline: US pact controlling 65bn barrels of Venezuelan crude alters medium-term supply expectations for oil importers
items.what_happened: The US reached an agreement to take control over 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves, intended to revive Venezuela's production.
items.why_it_matters: Bringing heavy Venezuelan crude back under US management expands global supply capacity, dampening long-term upside risks for Brent crude and easing India's energy import bill.

items.headline: RBI schedules ₹27,000 crore state debt auction, testing duration appetite across long-tenor G-secs
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank of India announced an aggregate auction of ₹27,000 crore in State Government Securities, including re-issuances of long-term paper such as the 2046 Assam loan.
items.why_it_matters: Substantial state bond supply absorbs domestic institutional liquidity and could widen the spread between State Development Loans and benchmark central government securities.

items.headline: Finance Ministry sets October 12 pre-Budget timeline with emphasis on fiscal restraint and revenue targets
items.what_happened: The Ministry of Finance has scheduled pre-Budget meetings for the 2027-28 Union Budget starting October 12, 2026, directing central ministries to control spending and refine revenue estimates.
items.why_it_matters: Signals the government's ongoing commitment to the fiscal consolidation glide path, shaping central capex allocations and potential direct/indirect tax rationalization.
